title: Ardhanarishvara: the lord who is half woman
hook: the creator's world won't grow until Shiva appears as half himself, half the goddess: God and God's power in one body
carry: shiva and shakti are never two
tomorrow: why is the dancer's face so calm?

segments.voice: Yesterday in the Shiva Purana, three cities lined up and fell to one arrow: Shiva's fire burns what binds the soul. Today, the last selection.
screen: `HIS FIRE BURNS WHAT BINDS.` · `THE LAST SELECTION.`

segments.voice: A bronze figure stands with a slight sway at the hip. On its right side: a man's flat chest, matted hair piled high, a snake for an earring. On the left: a woman's breast, smooth braided hair, a round earring, an anklet on the foot, the hip curving out. Not two figures standing close. One figure, split down the middle. This is Ardhanarishvara, and the Shiva Purana tells a story about why the creator needed to see it.
screen: `RIGHT SIDE: MATTED HAIR, A SNAKE.` → `LEFT SIDE: BRAID, EARRING, ANKLET.` → `ONE FIGURE, SPLIT DOWN THE MIDDLE.`

segments.voice: Brahma, the creator, has a problem. He makes beings from his own mind, and they don't multiply. The world stays small. So he does tapas, and Shiva appears to him in this form, half himself and half the goddess. Brahma bows and asks the goddess side for help. She gives a power of her own so that creation can go on, and in the story the world begins to grow through women and men together. So the picture isn't a riddle. It's an answer: creation doesn't go forward on one half. The name says it plainly: ardha, half, nari, woman, ishvara, lord. The lord who is half woman. Some Shaiva teachers put it this way: Shiva and Shakti, the god and his power, are never really two. One poet found an image for it. At the opening of his long poem the Raghuvamsha, Kalidasa bows to Parvati and Shiva, the parents of the world, joined, he says, like a word and its meaning. Try separating those. A word with no meaning is noise; a meaning with no word can't be said. So the teaching is plain: in Shaiva and Shakta thought, God isn't only male, and Shakti, the power that makes and moves the world, isn't a lesser half. It's God's own power. It's why, in Hindi, a wife can be called ardhangini, the half of the body, and why many rites are done by husband and wife together. That's the last selection from the Shiva Purana: Sati and Parvati, who circled Shiva through all those stories, now standing in one body with him.
screen: `BRAHMA'S WORLD WON'T GROW.` · `HALF SHIVA, HALF THE GODDESS.` · `LIKE A WORD AND ITS MEANING.` · `SHAKTI IS GOD'S OWN POWER.` · then, large: `SHIVA AND SHAKTI ARE NEVER TWO.`

segments.voice: Bring your attention to the right side of the body, the hand, the shoulder, the foot, and breathe there a few breaths; then move to the left side and breathe there. Then let the line down the middle go soft, and feel the whole body breathing as one thing. If you pray, you can say the names Shiva and Shakti, or the name of God you use, and let them rest together.
The Shiva Purana. Today's selection, and the last: Ardhanarishvara, the lord who is half woman, the answer when Brahma's world wouldn't grow.
Your line: Shiva and Shakti are never two. Tomorrow, Shiva dances. That's the Shiva Purana, gathered up.

screen: `DAY 1124 COUNTS.` → `THE SHIVA PURANA, COMPLETE.` → `TOMORROW: WHY IS THE DANCER'S FACE SO CALM?`
